unavailable_fields.compute_overlap_ms: not_applicable: single-device task; no communication intervals to overlap with compute intervals
unavailable_fields.communication_without_compute_ms: not_applicable: single-device task; no communication intervals
unavailable_fields.nccl_algorithm_protocol_channel_selectio: unavailable: nccl_tuning requires communication enabled and at least 2 devices; kernel entry names alone do not identify the protocol and none exist here
unavailable_fields.per_collective_pcie_nvlink_bytes: unavailable: no hardware traffic counters are collected; device_telemetry readings are device-wide with native windows, and memcpy or logical payload sizes are not PCIe/NVLink wire traffic (kept unknown, never inferred)
unavailable_fields.cross_rank_submit_spread_us: unavailable: single rank; cross-rank spread requires matched participants and shared clock evidence (cross_rank matched is empty)
unavailable_fields.gpu_metric_tables: unavailable: profiling.gpu_counters is not enabled in the request, so nsys runs without --gpu-metrics-devices; counter probe remains not_requested

plan.rationale: Single-process, single-device FP32 GraphSAGE forward (request.json: 1 device, distributed_backend null, communication not_applicable in observations.json), so nccl_tuning, device_telemetry and collective_calibration have no collectives to characterize and are excluded. The torch collector already ran and fully associated all 15 CUDA kernels with 0 unassociated and 0 ambiguous forward sequences (coverage.json), so re-profiling and execution_timeline's submit/cross-rank evidence add nothing: its distinctive c10d CPU-submit association, gradient-bucket callbacks and clock-alignment bounds require communication or multiple ranks, and its per-device kernel interval summary is derivable from the nsys export. Trace evidence shows index_add_ (~375us) plus index_select (~212us) dominating linear (~90us), with clean median latency 0.781ms versus 724.7us of hook-perturbed diagnostic CUDA time on the 7168-node/143360-edge workload; the discovery run's profiled wall was 6.57ms, confirming heavy profiler perturbation. The open questions for the latency objective are therefore clean-timeline questions: per-kernel nanosecond intervals without torch-profiler/discovery hooks, kernel active union versus span (inter-kernel gaps and launch overlap, i.e. device-bound versus launch-bound), per-module attribution via NVTX ranges for model.first/model.second, and whether node-level CUDA-graph tracing is supported for capture-based follow-ups. Nsys is installed (request.json tools.nsys) and is the single collector that resolves exactly these overlap, graph-tracing and attribution questions, so it is the only addition requested. python_runtime is excluded because cProfile perturbs execution and host time is already bounded as a small share of the synchronized 0.781ms window; it can be requested later if nsys shows launch-bound gaps. candidate_diagnostics is excluded because this revision has no installed candidate bundles yet (not_applicable). No PCIe/NVLink traffic is invented from payload or memcpy sizes, and no unavailable dimension is fabricated.
